INDICATIONS FOR CXR 
 
* Non-responders to initial   
   management 
* Hypoxic (O2 Sats < 92%) 
* Suspected pneumothorax 
* Suspected pneumonia 
* Chest pain 
* Cardiovascular instability 
* Possible aspirated foreign

* Uncertainty about asthma  
   being the cause of respiratory  
   distress

Contents

 
  ASTHMA IN THE ED 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
HIGH RISK PATIENTS 
* Previous near fatal exacerbation / intubation / ICU admission 
* Recent or current use of steroids 
* Co-morbid cardiac or respiratory pathology 
* Admission or ED visit in the last month 
* > 2 admissions in the last year 
* > 3 ED visits in the last year 
* Psychiatric patient 
* Illicit drug use 
* Use of > 2 full rescue inhalers (short acting b2 agonists) in last month 
INTUBATED PATIENT CONSIDERATIONS 
* Ventilator Settings 
 
MODE   
Volume Assist Control 
 
TV 
 
6ml/kg (4-6ml/kg) 
 
I:E ratio 
1:3 (may increase to 1:4 or 1:5 as needed) 
 
RR 
 
10 -12 bpm 
 
Alarm Pmax 
Readjust to allow for higher pressures initially 
* Preload with 20ml/kg IV fluids to avoid a precipitous drop in BP  
* Continue with inline nebulisations 
IF DETERIORATION AFTER INTUBATION CONSIDER 
* Displacement of ET tube  
* Obstruction of ET tube / mucous plug 
* Pneumothorax / pneumomediastinum 
* Equipment failure / disconnection 
* Suctioning required / stomach overdistension 
DISCHARGE CRITERIA 
*  Pulse < 110bpm, RR < 25 bpm, O2 Sats > 92% on room air 
* No high-risk patient features (see box) 
* Patient’s improvement and response is sustained ³ 1 hour after last  
   nebulisation 
* Peak flow > 75% of patient’s best / predicted 
DISPOSITION 
Severe
